mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (measured in percent) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level against 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% signals a tightening monetary policy that raises the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer spending, which increases corporate revenue visibility and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST growth > 0.5% and RSAFS growth > 0.5%) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), rising wage pressures and the subsequent expectation of monetary tightening lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns less than 60% of the time, or the difference in mean returns between low and high unemployment regimes is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales level (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which directly boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for RSAFS level against 5-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing contraction regime (INDPRO < 100), the risk of a recession increases, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns less than 60% of the time, or the difference in mean returns between INDPRO<100 and INDPRO>=100 is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals an overheating economy with both monetary tightening and tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and UNRATE < 4.0%) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p>0.05).
